overview: The Council approved technical zoning amendments, community preservation funding, and a clerical union contract. A significant portion of the meeting was dedicated to addressing resident grievances regarding illegal short-term rentals and the city's failure to enforce building codes and maintain distressed properties.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Meeting Records
items.summary: The Council offered condolences to the family of John Garrity, commended Hunt's Photo on its 134th anniversary, and approved the August 15, 2023 meeting minutes.

items.title: Waste Hauler Contract Report
items.summary: The Council approved a committee report authorizing the mayor to sign a 10-year waste hauler contract.

items.title: Zoning Ordinance Amendments
items.summary: Approved various technical corrections to the zoning ordinance, including changes to special permit requirements for inclusionary housing and restrictions on motor vehicle-related uses. The amendments were approved pending a six-day public comment period.

items.title: Clerical Union Wage Adjustments
items.summary: Approved contractual wage increases for clerical union employees covering the period from 2020 through 2023.

items.title: Community Preservation Committee Appropriations
items.summary: Authorized funding for four projects, including $800,000 for Walkland Court redevelopment and $400,000 for an accessible playground at the McGlynn School.

items.title: Food Truck Permit
items.summary: Approved a permit for the Chicken and Rice Guys food truck to operate during a festival at Riverbend Park in October.

items.title: Short-Term Rental Enforcement and Resident Complaints
items.summary: Resident Elliot Jockelson presented evidence of multiple zoning violations at 66 Lyman Avenue, leading the Council to pass a resolution requesting proactive enforcement and a formal liaison with rental platforms like Airbnb.

items.title: Handicapped Parking at Medford/Tufts T Station
items.summary: Referred a request to address the lack of ADA-compliant parking at the new T station to the Traffic and Disability Commissions after a resident reported being unable to find accessible parking for over a year.

items.title: Code Enforcement Staffing and Resource Plan
items.summary: Passed a resolution requesting a plan to increase inspectional services staffing and a secondary motion to explore using per diem or retired staff to assist with enforcement backlog.

items.title: Distressed Property and Legal Default at 41 Emory Street
items.summary: The Council demanded a written explanation from the administration for why city legal counsel failed to appear in court regarding the distressed property at 41 Emory Street. Resolution passed requesting immediate property cleanup and a full report on city legal oversight.

items.title: Take-Home Vehicle Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance to regulate the use and tracking of city-owned take-home vehicles to the Subcommittee on Ordinances and Rules.

items.title: Solidarity with Tufts Resident Assistants
items.summary: Approved a resolution standing in solidarity with the ULTRA workers union during their contract negotiations and strike action at Tufts University.

items.title: High Street Crosswalk and City Commissions
items.summary: Approved a request to repaint a crosswalk at 190 High Street and referred discussions regarding the creation of a Gender Equity Commission and a Youth Commission to subcommittee.

items.title: Waste Disposal Study
items.summary: Voted to ask the administration to study the placement of additional trash barrels along the Mystic River and within business districts to combat litter and rodent issues.
